company_name: Rio Tinto Limited (dual-listed with Rio Tinto plc)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (5.3%, FY2020-FY2025) tempered toward equity_5yr_cagr (5.7%) and a softening iron-ore price deck; for a commodity cyclical the driver paths are built from volume guidance and mid-cycle prices, not extrapolated from any CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.7% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 0.3% and revenue 3yr CAGR 1.2%: divergence >30%. Book value compounds from retained earnings while EPS and FCF are price-cycle driven (FY2021 iron-ore peak US$13.05 EPS vs US$6.14 FY2025).
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - consolidated capex) less the P&L share-based payment charge (FY2025 237, FY2024 172, FY2023 144; FY2022 ~130 and FY2020 ~120 estimated from the equity-statement credit x ~1.75). Owner-FCF CAGR (-22.8% / -14.9%) is only marginally below reported (-21.8% / -14.2%): SBC is 0.4% of revenue and not a driver here. The FCF decline is a capex supercycle (capex 14% -> 21% of revenue FY2020->FY2025) plus the iron-ore price normalising from the FY2021 peak, not an operating-margin collapse; OCF FY2025 US$16.8bn is above FY2020 US$15.9bn.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle: iron ore drifts to US$85-95/t through 2027 as Simandou supply arrives, while copper (Oyu Tolgoi to ~500ktpa 2028-36, Kennecott/Escondida), aluminium and a recovering lithium business take Copper+Aluminium+Lithium durably above half of group EBITDA. Revenue +10% in FY2026 on H1's price strength, roughly flat in FY2027, then 3.5-4.5% volume-led growth to FY2030 (~20% CuEq growth target). Cash-EBITDA margin 39-40% (vs 42% ex-boom average, 38% FY2023-25). Rio-share capex stays at the ~US$11bn guidance through FY2027 then falls to 13.5% of revenue as Simandou and the replacement mines complete. Cash tax 25% (FY2026 guided) then 30%, plus NCI leakage rising to 7% of EBIT as the partnered assets ramp. One 9% USD WACC, 2% terminal growth, 14x terminal cap. FY2025 FCF (US$4.5bn) is a capex-trough number, not the run-rate: year-1 unlevered owner FCF is ~US$9bn.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prices hold near H1 2026 levels across copper, aluminium and lithium, iron ore stays above US$95/t helped by a high-grade premium, projects land on time, productivity and asset sales pull capex down to 13% of revenue and the cash margin returns to 42-44%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Iron ore at US$75-80/t from 2027 (China steel demand, Simandou surplus), copper/aluminium mean-revert, lithium stays oversupplied, projects slip and capex stays at 14% of revenue; cash margin 33-35%, revenue -8% in FY2027 then +2%/yr.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Tier-1 diversified miner valued on mid-cycle cash-EBITDA margins rather than the current price deck, with the capex supercycle (Simandou, Oyu Tolgoi, lithium, Pilbara replacement) explicitly ramped down instead of anchoring on a trough FY2025 FCF. The engine's cash-EBITDA margin (OCF-reconciled) sits ~5.5pp below Rio's underlying EBITDA margin, which is the difference between a valuation that ties to the cash-flow statement and one that capitalises equity-accounted EBITDA and ignores closure spend. NCI (Simandou/Oyu Tolgoi partners) is charged once, in the flows. Value is stated per DLC share in USD and converted to AUD at spot; the ~22% Limited-over-plc premium is a franking artefact the model deliberately does not pay for. Cyclical risk lives in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight, not in an inflated WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Iron ore price: each US$10/t is ~US$3bn of EBITDA on ~330Mt Pilbara sales; the base deck (US$85-95/t) sits below spot but above the bear US$75-80/t
Copper/aluminium/lithium mean reversion from H1 2026 highs (a 10% move in copper, aluminium or AUD is ~US$1.1-1.3bn of EBITDA each)
Execution across Simandou, Oyu Tolgoi underground, three lithium ramps and three Pilbara replacement mines simultaneously; capex overrun keeps capex above the 13.5% long-run path
NCI leakage assumption (7% of EBIT by FY2031) depends on Simandou/Oyu Tolgoi economics; the Erdenes carry-loan recovery could make it lower, a Chinalco asset-for-equity swap could make it higher
Cash-EBITDA vs underlying EBITDA gap (~5.5pp) assumed persistent; if EAU dividends rise toward EAU EBITDA share or closure spend falls, the model is conservative
AUD/USD: RIO.AX value scales inversely with the AUD; a 10% stronger AUD cuts the AUD intrinsic value ~10% independent of operations
DLC premium: RIO.AX's ~22% premium to plc can widen or compress without any change in intrinsic value

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular ASX session, intraday); 52-week range 120.30-195.84 AUD. FX from Yahoo AUDUSD=X; parity check vs RIO (NYSE) and RIO.L in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: RIO.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2014-FY2025, H1 FY2024-26, USD millions, underlying EBITDA FY2018+); RIO.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt (income statement 14354-14378, cash flow 14440-14475, employment costs 17696, Rio share of capital investment 1671, NCI equity 14594); RIO.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (net debt note 3873-3958, borrowings 2930, cash 1968, capital investment 655-679, guidance 215-375).
data_sources.qualitative: RIO.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): segment mix, FY2026 guidance (H1 results 29 July 2026), Simandou/Oyu Tolgoi/lithium ramp, CMD Dec-2025 targets, bull/bear axes.

inputs.sbc_source: RIO.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:17696 employment-costs note, 'Share-based payment charge' US$237m FY2025 (US$172m FY2024, US$144m FY2023), note 28. No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed (UK/AU plans are settled by on-market purchase, US$57m FY2025, a financing outflow); the P&L charge is used as the full cost. Metrics.csv StockBasedComp was empty; the three disclosed years were backfilled via make fix.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in USD; RIO.AX (Rio Tinto Limited CDI) quotes in AUD. Per-share values computed in USD and converted at AUDUSD 0.7016 (USD->AUD 1.4253), Yahoo AUDUSD=X 2026-09-25T04:34Z. Parity check against the plc line: RIO (NYSE, 1 ADR = 1 plc share) US$94.47 at 2026-09-24 close x 1.4253 = A$134.65 vs RIO.AX A$164.83, i.e. the Limited line trades at a ~22% premium to plc. The direction and magnitude of the rate are confirmed by the check; the residual is the long-standing DLC franking premium, which this model does NOT capitalise: intrinsic value is the economic value of one share of the DLC, so RIO.AX screens as more expensive than the identical plc share.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:13:18Z (intraday, regular ASX session; refresh at the 06:00Z close)
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares H1 2026, 1,640.2m (plc + Limited combined, RIO.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt); basic 1,624m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks have been zero since FY2020, and no non-SBC issuance is planned.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Rio Tinto's own net debt definition, note 20 of the H1 2026 interim: total borrowings US$21,414m + lease liabilities ~US$1,650m - cash US$8,913m - other liquid resources ~US$90m = US$14,061m at 30 June 2026 (31 Dec 2025: US$14,362m). total_debt is stated as net_debt + cash so the two tie. Includes the ~US$9.7bn of borrowings taken on for the March 2025 Arcadium Lithium acquisition. Equity attributable to NCI (US$4.8bn at FY2025) is NOT deducted here: NCI is charged once, in the flows (see nci_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 = cost of equity ~9.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (A/A2 rated) on ~10% debt weight (net debt US$14bn vs ~US$155bn market equity) = WACC ~9.0%. Commodity cyclicality is charged in the bear scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not by stacking a premium on WACC; one WACC across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (~US$1.65bn, ~1% of EV) sit inside Rio's net debt figure and lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; lease interest is already inside operating cash flow and hence inside the cash-EBITDA margin. Right-of-use renewal is covered by a long-run capex path (13.5% of revenue) held above D&A (12%). lease_cost_pct_path is therefore zero. Immaterial at Rio's scale but stated so a later update does not switch treatments.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows. Revenue and EBITDA are consolidated (100% of Oyu Tolgoi, SimFer/Simandou, IOC) while capex is on Rio's own 'share of capital investment' basis (FY2025 US$11,403m vs US$12,335m consolidated; partners fund their share). The NCI share of after-tax profit is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a leakage on EBIT: ~2% in FY2026 (FY2025 NCI profit US$283m and NCI dividends US$314m on EBIT ~US$18.8bn = 1.5-1.7%), rising to 7% by FY2031 as Simandou (Rio economic interest ~45% of SimFer's mine) and Oyu Tolgoi (34% Erdenes) ramp: ~US$1.7bn of NCI profit on ~US$17bn NOPAT. The US$4.8bn NCI book equity is not deducted in the bridge (that would charge it twice). FY0 check: FY2025 attributable net income US$9,966m vs component NOPAT at FY2025 drivers (cash EBITDA 22.2bn - D&A 6.6bn) x (1-0.29) = US$11.1bn, the gap being after-tax net interest (~US$0.6bn) and items excluded from underlying earnings; ties within noise.
inputs.ebitda_definition: IMPORTANT: ebitda_margin_path is a CASH-EBITDA margin, defined as (operating cash flow + tax paid + net interest paid + NCI dividends) / revenue, NOT Rio's 'underlying EBITDA'. It runs ~5.5pp below underlying EBITDA (FY2025 38.6% vs 44.0%; FY2024 38.4% vs 43.4%; FY2023 37.9% vs 44.2%; FY2022 43.0% vs 47.3%; FY2021 55.9% vs 59.4%; FY2020 50.2% vs 53.6%; FY2019 46.9% vs 49.1%; FY2018 40.1% vs 44.8%) because underlying EBITDA includes Rio's share of equity-accounted units' EBITDA (Escondida etc., vs US$1.07bn of dividends actually received), excludes ~US$1bn/yr of closure-provision cash spend, and ignores working-capital absorption. Building from underlying EBITDA would overstate owner FCF by ~US$3bn/yr; the cash basis makes the component build reconcile to reported OCF. 8-year average 43.9%, ex-FY2021 42.2%, FY2023-25 38.3%, H1 2026 ~38.7% (H1 runs 2-3pp below full year seasonally). Sanity multiples that use Metrics.csv EBITDA are on the underlying basis.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 2: operating company, non-US and cyclical), with the adaptations file applied: USD-built WACC, USD->AUD quote conversion with parity check, leases treatment A, NCI charged once in the flows, risk charged once (flows + weights, not WACC). Not a peak-earnings extrapolation: FY2025/H1-2026 is a strong copper/aluminium/lithium price environment (H1 2026 underlying EBITDA +28%) against a softening iron-ore market; margins are set to a mid-cycle cash basis (base 39-40% vs 8-yr average ex-boom 42%). The FY2025 reported FCF (US$4.5bn) is depressed by a capex supercycle (Simandou, Oyu Tolgoi, lithium, Pilbara replacement mines: consolidated capex US$12.3bn, 21% of revenue vs a 10-year norm of ~13%), so a trailing-FCF anchor would understate the business; capex is ramped down to 13.5% of revenue by FY2031 as Simandou completes. Buybacks: zero since FY2020 (dividends US$6-15bn/yr are the distribution channel); the flat count is a modelling convention Rio funds through small on-market purchases for employee plans (US$57m FY2025). Interest income (finance income US$465m) is NOT stripped: Rio is a net-debt company and the unlevered engine excludes both interest legs while netting cash in net debt. Simandou first sales April 2026 and Arcadium (Mar-2025) are in the growth path as volume, not as separate bridge items. DLC: intrinsic value is per DLC share converted at spot; the ~22% Limited-over-plc premium is not modelled.

bear.narrative: China's property-led steel demand keeps sliding, record port inventories and steel export licensing bite, and Simandou's own 120Mtpa system (Rio's plus WCS) tips seaborne iron ore into surplus: prices settle at US$75-80/t from 2027, cutting Pilbara EBITDA by a third. Copper and aluminium mean-revert from H1 2026 highs and lithium stays oversupplied, so revenue falls 8% in FY2027 and grows only 2% thereafter. Concurrent mega-project execution (Oyu Tolgoi underground, Simandou rail/port after two fatalities, three lithium ramps, Pilbara replacement mines) slips, keeping capex at 14% of revenue and lifting D&A. Cash-EBITDA margin compresses to 33-35% (FY2016 was 32.7%). Rio survives comfortably (16% gearing, A-rated) but the diversification premium in the price evaporates.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +10%: H1 2026 revenue +15.5% YoY (copper +39%, aluminium +33%, lithium +125% average prices; iron ore flat at US$92.6/t realised) with a softer H2 iron-ore price. FY2027 +1%: consensus iron ore US$85-100/t (-8% price) largely offset by Simandou volume (SimFer consolidated ~20-25Mt), Oyu Tolgoi ramp (>30% H1 2026 copper growth) and lithium (Fenix/Sal de Vida/Rincon toward ~200ktpa LCE by 2028). FY2028-30 +3.5-4.5%: Simandou toward 60Mt SimFer share, Oyu Tolgoi ~500ktpa 2028-36, ~20% CuEq growth 2024-30 (management target), Pilbara replacement mines hold Pilbara flat. FY2031+ 2.5% nominal, terminal 2.0% (depleting asset base, USD inflation).
base.margin_note: Cash-EBITDA basis (see inputs.ebitda_definition). FY2026 40.5% = H1 38.7% plus the normal H2 seasonal uplift; FY2027-28 39% as iron ore softens; drifts to 40% by FY2030 on copper mix (Oyu Tolgoi C1 30-50c/lb) and the US$1.8bn productivity run-rate, still ~2pp below the ex-FY2021 8-year average of 42%.
base.tax_note: Cash tax 25% FY2026 (guided ETR ~25% on DTA utilisation) reverting to 30% from FY2027 (guided), plus NCI leakage 2% -> 7% of EBIT by FY2031 (inputs.nci_treatment). Combined 27% -> 37%.
base.capex_note: Rio share of capital investment: FY2026 guidance up to US$11bn (growth up to 3.0, sustaining ~4.0, replacement 3-4, decarbonisation ~0.2) = 17.4% of FY2026 revenue; FY2027 held ~US$11bn (three Pilbara replacement mines first ore 2027, Simandou, Rincon); then down to 13.5% by FY2031 (sustaining ~4 + replacement ~3 + growth ~2 on ~US$75bn revenue), above D&A at 12%.
base.wc_note: Receivables + inventory exceed payables for a miner; -5% capture on the revenue change.

bull.narrative: Copper, aluminium and lithium prices hold near H1 2026 levels (electrification, grid and data-centre demand; lithium recovery sustained) and iron ore holds US$95-105/t as high-grade Simandou ore earns a premium in a decarbonising steel industry; Oyu Tolgoi reaches ~500ktpa on schedule, Simandou ramps to 60Mt SimFer share by 2029 without further major incidents; the US$1.8bn+ productivity program and US$5-10bn asset-release plan (Borates, Iron & Titanium) fund growth so capex falls to 13% of revenue. Cash-EBITDA margin returns to the ex-boom 8-year average of 42-44%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: iron ore is still 48% of EBITDA with a structurally softening outlook that Rio's own Simandou volumes worsen, 57% of revenue is China, and the current H1 2026 earnings base rests on copper/aluminium/lithium prices at or near cycle highs. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs prices across three commodities to hold AND five concurrent mega-projects to deliver on schedule after fatalities at Simandou and Kennecott. Balance-sheet risk is low (16% gearing, A-rated) so the bear is a margin case, not a solvency case, which is why it is not higher. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
